correctness.rationale: In the normalized cube average all conjugations are immaterial for this real cosine. Expansion gives 256 signed forms on four cube inputs; the identical one-coordinate averages multiply across the n coordinates. An independent exact enumeration searched all integer minors to determine each rank and took the lexicographically first nonzero principal minor of that rank to represent its discriminant. It reproduced the entire table at RESULT.md:40–48, with only powers of two up to sign for nonzero determinants. Larger minors vanish over the integers, and a maximal nonzero principal minor survives reduction at every odd p, so both the rank and the representative used in the Gauss evaluation are justified. Completing squares on the nondegenerate quotient gives the normalized factor p^(−r/2) ε_p^r χ_p(Δ); summation gives even-rank contributions (44+24ν)/q and (26+32ν)/q², with the odd ranks cancelling for ν=−1 and contributing the stated η terms for ν=1. The two rank-zero terms give the baseline 1/128. In the negative branch the scaled correction is the cubic −16t³+68t²−112t+58 at t=√q>1, negative at t=1 with everywhere-negative derivative. The other branches are positive, and substitution verifies both small-field examples.
residual_risks: The rank replay certifies the finite integer input, not the Gauss-sum theorem or other quadratic forms. The baseline is the rank-zero term of this expansion, not an assumption of independent cosine values at the eight vertices.
